pr_title: http: reduce likelihood of race conditions on keep-alive timeout
pr_body:
This is the continued work from https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/52653 to fix many similar issues when request is near socket `keepAliveTimeout` threshold. Added 1 second internal timeout to account for network latency for both server and client side.

Fixes: https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/52649
Refs: https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/54293

issue_context.title: http: keepalive race condition near timeout
comments:
I'm experiencing this exact issue when trying to run `ionic start` to start a new ionic project.

![image](https://github.com/nodejs/node/assets/17459105/544f10a2-4199-41a4-928a-dc5f885ffc93)

@EthanTuning it's possible though unlikely related to this issue. ECONNRESET is a fairly general error code for when the server closes the socket unexpectedly. This issue is concerned with when an ECONNRESET occurs in the exact same tick of the event loop as a http request resuming on an previously used socket - which seems unlikely to be reproduced repeatedly except in the kind of narrow circumstances proposed in my post.

> The serverHintTimeout < agentTimeout conditional always evaluates to false (in the default conditions) because the default agentTimeout is 0 -- which means Node will never opportunistically close a connection and instead always wait for the server to close it first.

I think we should close them actually. PR?

> @EthanTuning it's possible though unlikely related to this issue. ECONNRESET is a fairly general error code for when the server closes the socket unexpectedly. This issue is concerned with when an ECONNRESET occurs in the exact same tick of the event loop as a http request resuming on an previously used socket - which seems unlikely to be reproduced repeatedly except in the kind of narrow circumstances proposed in my post.

Oh thanks, yeah I was very unsure, but googling got me here haha!

> The `serverHintTimeout < agentTimeout` conditional always evaluates to false (in the default conditions) because the default `agentTimeout` is 0 -- which means Node will never opportunistically close a connection and instead always wait for the server to close it first.

I realize default in this context meant two different things.

Using the default http.globalAgent -- the default timeout is 5000ms.
Using a non-default agent, with keepAlive on, but otherwise default parameters, (ie- `new http.Agent({ keepAlive: true });` -- the issue arises.

review_comments: You can simplify and potentially improve this code by checking if hint bigger than 0 or !NaN and just return 0 as timeout before calling parseInt and multiplying it with 1000.

I agree with you that this can be simplified, but I am not sure if the `NumberParseInt` can be early avoided. The `hint` comes back from regex, and is always a string. It will need to be checked with the `1000` before going to the conditions

@jazelly I had a test case failing after the node 20.18.0 upgrade, where the server's keep-alive timeout was set to 1000 ms, but with this change it's reduced by 1 second, so by setting it to <= 1000 ms you now effectively configure it as 0 which then effectively disable keep-alive, if i understood the code correctly?

BTW what happened in my test case is that it would check that a connection was re-used which suddenly didn't happen anymore. Once I bumped the server's keep-alive timeout from 1 second to 2 seconds, it was working again 🤷🏻‍♂️

Yes, that's because of this commit. Your understanding is correct.

There is a TODO to expose this as an configurable option. I just need to find time to do that, or anyone who would like to give it a swing is more than welcome to raise a PR. : )
